chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi'l-Qasim narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Qurashi, from Nasr ibn Muzahim, from Umar ibn Sa'd, from Yusuf ibn Yazid, from Abdullah ibn Awf ibn al-Ahmar.

He said: When the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) intended to set out to Nahrawan, an astrologer came to him and said to him: 'O Commander of the Faithful, do not travel at this hour — travel after three hours have passed from the day.' So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Why is that?' He said: 'Because if you travel at this hour, you and your companions will be afflicted with severe harm. But if you travel in the hour I have commanded you to go in, you will triumph, prevail, and obtain all that you seek.'

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Do you know what is in the belly of this beast — is it male or female?' He said: 'If I calculate, I will know.' Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Whoever ratifies you in this saying has belied the Quran.'

'Indeed Allah — with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in which land it will die. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.' [Quran 31:34]

'Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) would not claim what you are claiming. Do you allege that you can guide to the hour that steers one away from harm, and [identify] the hour that, if one travels in it, harm befalls him? Whoever ratifies you in this has become needless of seeking Allah's help for that matter, and made it more necessary to turn to you to repel harm from him, and it befits him to direct praise to you instead of to his Lord. So whoever believes in you in this has taken you as a rival and opponent to Allah.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Allah, there is no omen except Your omen, and there is no harm except Your harm, and there is no good except Your good, and there is no god but You.' Then he turned to the astrologer and said: 'Rather, we belie you and oppose you. We will travel in the hour that you have prohibited.'

key_terms.الِاسْتِعَانَةِ بِاللَّهِ: seeking Allah's help (istiana) — the act of turning to Allah for assistance
key_terms.الْمُنَجِّمُ: the astrologer — one who claims to predict events from star positions
key_terms.عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ: knowledge of the Hour — one of the five exclusive divine prerogatives in Quran 31:34
key_terms.لَا طَيْرَ إِلَّا طَيْرُكَ: there is no omen except Your omen — a prayer affirming that only Allah controls fortune and misfortune
key_terms.نِدًّا وَضِدًّا: rival and opponent — one who sets himself in competition with Allah, i.e., shirk

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say when an astrologer warned him before the Battle of Nahrawan?
ai.summary: Abdullah ibn Awf ibn al-Ahmar reports that when Imam Ali (AS) was preparing to march against the Kharijites at Nahrawan (38 AH/658 CE), an astrologer came to warn him that the stars were unfavorable at that hour and urged him to delay. Imam Ali tested the astrologer's claim by asking whether he could determine the sex of an animal from its stars — the astrologer claimed he could if he calculated. Imam Ali rejected this, citing Quran 31:34 (the five keys of the unseen) to show that such knowledge belongs to Allah alone. He then delivered a sharp theological rebuttal: whoever trusts an astrologer over Allah has effectively made the astrologer a partner to Allah (shirk). He concluded with a supplication affirming divine sovereignty, then deliberately set out in the very hour the astrologer had declared inauspicious.
